phase_task.goal: Stretch capabilities, in priority order: (0) fix the sandbox container-leak at its source; (1) self-repair from REAL sandbox failure output — the agent reads the actual captured error and produces a corrected patch within budget; (2) multi-file change — extend/rename a symbol used across many files, updating every call site and its tests. Build on the Phase-4 loop, journal, and sandbox unchanged in contract.

deliverables.d: UNIT 0 (prerequisite) — root-fix the container leak: give each sandbox run a unique --name; on wall-clock timeout (and any error path) explicitly docker stop/rm the NAMED container rather than only killing the docker-run client and relying on --rm. Prove it: a timed-out verification leaves ZERO leaked containers (assert count before==after). The make sandbox-clean trap remains as defense-in-depth, but the source leak must be gone. This is required because self-repair multiplies verify cycles and timeouts.

Self-repair loop: on a failed verification, the loop feeds the REAL captured sandbox failure output (Phase-3 stdout/stderr/exit) back into the model — in the DATA channel, never the instruction channel — and the agent proposes a corrected patch. Bounded by the same step/token/wall-clock budgets; repair attempts are journaled steps like any other (resumable, apply-once, no double-charge). A repair that exhausts budget ends budget-exhausted with partial progress; a repair that cannot fix ends give-up-with-reason. Deterministic stub drives a scripted fail-then-repair trajectory.

Multi-file change: using the Phase-1 references/call-graph, a rename/extend touches the definition AND every resolved call site AND the associated tests, as span/patch ops across files, verified as a single sandbox run. The rename target is the Phase-1 planted cross-file symbol (serialize_user / formatUser).

Conflict handling (harden the Phase-4 minimal approach): two concurrent tasks committing to the same workspace are serialized or safely rejected — never silent clobber. State the mechanism (base-commit check + advisory lock / WAL BEGIN IMMEDIATE). A losing writer is rejected cleanly or rebased-and-reverified, not dropped.
Wire into agentctl for operator inspection (self-repair trajectory + multi-file diff visible in the trace).

phase_task.oracle: Via make test (deterministic stub for logic; real Docker for the verify/repair mechanism): (0) a verification that hits the wall-clock deadline leaves zero leaked containers — assert container count before==after around a timeout run; (1) SELF-REPAIR: a task whose first patch fails tests reads the REAL failure output and produces a corrected patch that then passes in the sandbox → verified-success; assert the repair input contained the actual error text (from Phase-3 capture) and arrived via the data channel; (2) a self-repair task given an unfixable failure ends give-up-with-reason (not fabricated success) within budget; (3) a self-repair task with too small a budget ends budget-exhausted at a clean journaled checkpoint, workspace uncorrupted, and RESUMES without re-charging prior repair steps; (4) MULTI-FILE: renaming the planted cross-file symbol updates the definition + all N resolved call sites + tests, and the single sandbox run passes → assert every expected call site changed (programmatic diff check) and none missed; (5) CONCURRENCY: two tasks committing to the same workspace do not silently clobber — one wins, the other is rejected/rebased, and the final state is consistent (assert no lost write); (6) determinism/replay preserved across the new repair steps.
phase_task.docs: DESIGN.md: extend the agent-loop section with the self-repair cycle (real-failure-output-in-data-channel → corrected patch, bounded, journaled) and the multi-file change strategy (call-graph-driven span edits across files + tests, single verification). Update the isolation/concurrency section with the hardened conflict handling and state the guarantee (serialize or reject, no silent clobber). Note the container-leak root fix in the sandbox section / ADR-0003 (supersedes the Phase-4 janitor-only mitigation). Update the "what we cut / would do next" if scope shifts.
phase_task.stop: Do not start Phase 6 (API/auth/metering wrapper). Report: the container-leak root fix and its zero-leak proof; the self-repair data-flow (how real sandbox output reaches the model in the data channel, bounded + journaled); the multi-file edit strategy and the diff-check proving all call sites updated; the concurrency conflict mechanism and its no-lost-write proof; and confirmation that resume/apply-once/no-double-charge still hold across repair steps.
